title: Scout Results Plots (All Runs)
description: Schema for the PDF figures in the ./results/plots for any run configuration.
notes: Structure: adoption scenario folder -> metric folder (energy, co2, cost)
-> the three figures in that folder (byECM, Aggregate, CostEffective).
Run options that change the figures:
alt_regions: energy in TWh (EMM), TBtu (State), or Quads (AIA);
site_energy: 'Site Energy' with no site-source tag;
captured_energy: 'CE S-S' instead of 'FF S-S';
health_costs: snapshot year 2020 and energy in Quads;
tsv_metrics: energy in GWh or GW, CO2 in Tt, cost in Million $,
and a suffix such as ', Pk. Prd. Sum. (S)' in the axis labels;
adopt_scn_restrict: only one adoption scenario folder is plotted.
No figures are written when run.py uses trim_vars or report_custom_yrs.

max_adopt_potential.description: Measures capture their applicable markets as baseline stock turns over.

tech_potential.description: Measures capture their full applicable markets immediately.

scenario.description: Contents of one adoption scenario folder.

metricFolder.description: Contents of one metric folder (energy, co2, or cost).
notes: The three folders share this definition; names and labels differ only by metric.

byECM.description: Annual energy use, CO₂ emissions, or energy cost for each measure.
notes: Reference case vs. with measure,
each with and without measure competition.
The first is 'All ECMs' (competed totals summed across all measures).

Aggregate.description: Competed savings summed across all measures.

panels.description: Three stacked panels of competed savings across all measures.
notes: Broken out by region, building class, and end use.

CostEffective.description: Measure cost effectiveness vs. competed savings.
notes: Savings: competed savings in the snapshot year.
Metrics: for one unit installed in the snapshot year, over the measure lifetime,
assuming that year's savings every year.
Each point is a measure with non-zero savings
Codes/standards measures are excluded.

snapshot_year.description: Single year shown in this figure; appears in the x-axis label.
notes: Savings (x): competed savings in this year only, not cumulative.
Metrics (y): for one unit installed in this year, over the measure lifetime.
2050 by default; 2020 for public health cost (PHC) runs.

panels.description: One scatter panel per financial metric.
notes: In this order: IRR, payback, CCE, CCC.
Lines: reference case uncompeted (thick grey),
with measure uncompeted (light grey),
reference case competed and with measure competed
(navy and light blue for technical potential;
red and pink for max adoption potential),
The 'All ECMs' panel has meaningful competed lines only.

range.description: First and last modeled year plotted.
notes: The first year depends on the baseline data; the last is 2050.

y_axis.description: Annual energy use, CO₂ emissions, or energy cost.

aggregatePanel.description: Annual savings for each breakout category with non-zero savings.
notes: the annual total (solid dark grey),
and the cumulative total on a right-hand axis (dotted grey).
The panel is blank if total savings are zero.

title.pattern: ^(Energy Savings|Avoided CO₂|Cost Savings) by (Region|Building Class|End Use)$

range.description: First and last modeled year plotted.
notes: The first year depends on the baseline data; the last is 2050.

y2_axis.description: Right axis: cumulative savings from the first modeled year.

costEffPanel.description: Scatter of measures: competed savings (x) vs. financial metric (y).
notes: A dotted line marks the cost-effectiveness threshold;
the cost-effective side is shaded.
The five cost-effective measures with the largest savings
are numbered on the plot and listed in the top-right corner.

x_axis.description: Competed savings in the snapshot year.

cost_effective_region.description: Shaded side of the threshold where measures count as cost effective.

cost_effective_impact.description: Top-left label: total savings of the cost-effective measures.

top_measures.description: Top-right list of up to five cost-effective measures.
notes: Ranked by savings, as '<rank> <measure name>'.
